(course page, with the slides and the downloads: <https://sophiedonnet.github.io/urban_networks.html>).

::: {.callout-note title="References"}
**Data**

- Baldock, K. C. R., Goddard, M. A., Hicks, D. M., Kunin, W. E., Mitschunas, N., Morse, H.,
  Osgathorpe, L. M., Potts, S. G., Robertson, K. M., Scott, A. V., Staniczenko, P. P. A.,
  Stone, G. N., Vaughan, I. P. & Memmott, J. (2019). A systems approach reveals urban pollinator
  hotspots and conservation opportunities. *Nature Ecology & Evolution*, 3, 363–373.
  [doi:10.1038/s41559-018-0769-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-018-0769-y)
- Insect taxonomy completed with the compilation of Doré, M., Fontaine, C. & Thébault, E. (2021).
  Relative effects of anthropogenic pressures, climate, and sampling design on the structure of
  pollination networks at the global scale. *Global Change Biology*, 27(6), 1266–1280.
  [doi:10.1111/gcb.15474](https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.15474)

**R packages**

- `sbm`: Chiquet, J., Donnet, S. & Barbillon, P. *sbm: Stochastic Blockmodels*. R package,
  [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sbm) ·
  [GitHub](https://github.com/GrossSBM/sbm)
- `colSBM`: SBM for collections of networks. R package,
  [GitHub](https://github.com/GrossSBM/colSBM).
  Method: Chabert-Liddell, S.-C., Barbillon, P. & Donnet, S. (2024). Learning common structures
  in a collection of networks. An application to food webs. *The Annals of Applied Statistics*,
  18(2), 1213–1235. [doi:10.1214/23-AOAS1831](https://doi.org/10.1214/23-AOAS1831)

  Bipartite networks: Lacoste, L., Barbillon, P. & Donnet, S. (2025). Common structure discovery
  in collections of bipartite networks: application to pollination systems. Preprint,
  [arXiv:2512.01716](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01716) ·
  [HAL: hal-05399136](https://hal.science/hal-05399136v1)
:::

This document follows the sections of the slides and gives, for each figure, table or number
of the slides, the R code that produces it.  

The estimations are long (up to 1 h for a colSBM):
they are cached in `results_analysis/`. Delete a file to re-estimate it.

The estimations can be launched with the scripts in the folder `scripts/`.

# Setup

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(sbm)       # SBM on one network
library(colSBM)    # SBM on a collection of networks (>= 0.4.11, GitHub GrossSBM/colSBM)
library(bipartite) # d' specialisation index
library(vegan)     # NODF

col_plant <- "#66C1BF"; col_poll <- "#FFA500"   # colours of the slides
cols_status <- c(Native = col_plant, `Non-native` = col_poll, Mixed = "grey55", unknown = "grey85")
cols_group <- c(Bee = "#F2D04B", Hoverfly = "#D45E00", `Other Diptera` = "#7A5195",
                Beetle = "#2F7F5F", `Butterfly / moth` = "#3E7CB1", `Other Hymenoptera` = "grey60")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14))

# estimate once, then read the cached result
cached_fit <- function(file, expr) {
  if (file.exists(file)) return(readRDS(file))
  set.seed(1)
  fit <- expr
  saveRDS(fit, file)
  fit
}
```

# Motivation: the data

Baldock et al. (2019), *Nature Ecology & Evolution* 3: 363–373. 4 cities (Bristol, Edinburgh,
Leeds, Reading) × 9 land uses, 360 sites. One record = one insect caught on one flower.
The networks are built from the supplementary files of the paper (in `data_Baldock2019/`, see its
`README.md` for the choices made) by `scripts/01_build_networks_Baldock2019.R`, which writes
`data_Baldock2019/baldock2019_networks.rds`.

```{r data}
baldock <- readRDS("data_Baldock2019/baldock2019_networks.rds")
head(baldock$records, 3)
nrow(baldock$records)   # number of visits

# a network = a table plants x insects, counting the visits
net_city <- lapply(split(baldock$records, baldock$records$city),
                   function(d) unclass(table(d$plant, d$insect)))
all.equal(lapply(net_city, function(M) sum(M)), lapply(baldock$net_city, sum))
net_city <- baldock$net_city
```

Plant status (native / non-native) and insect groups:

```{r species info}
plant_status <- setNames(baldock$plants$status, baldock$plants$plant)
plant_status[is.na(plant_status)] <- "unknown"
insect_group <- setNames(baldock$insects$group, baldock$insects$insect)
```

# Introduction to networks

## Graphs and matrices: the Bristol network

```{r bristol}
M <- net_city$Bristol           # counts: plants x insects
B <- 1 * (M > 0)                # binary incidence matrix
c(plants = nrow(M), insects = ncol(M), links = sum(B), visits = sum(M))
```

Slide *"Bristol: the count matrix"* and *"the weighted network"*: the count matrix, and the
distribution of the counts per pair (plant, insect).

```{r bristol counts, fig.height = 5}
pairs <- as.data.frame(as.table(M)) |> setNames(c("plant", "insect", "visits")) |> filter(visits > 0)
pairs |> slice_max(visits, n = 4)       # the largest counts
mean(pairs$visits == 1)                 # share of the pairs seen once

plotMyMatrix(log1p(M), dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "insects")) +   # log scale: counts 1 to 81
  ggplot(pairs, aes(visits)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "number of visits per pair (plant, insect)", y = "number of pairs")
```

The bipartite graph and the binarised incidence matrix:

```{r bristol graph, fig.height = 5}
plotweb(B, sorting = "dec", box_size = 0.03, higher_labels = rep("", ncol(B)), lower_labels = rep("", nrow(B)),
        higher_color = col_poll, lower_color = col_plant, link_color = "grey60", link_alpha = 0.3)
plotMyMatrix(B, dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "insects"))
```

## Node-level descriptors

Degree (number of partners) and strength (number of visits), slides *"Degree"*,
*"Strength"*, *"Degree vs strength"*.

```{r degree strength, fig.height = 4}
nodes <- bind_rows(
  tibble(type = "plants", species = rownames(M), degree = rowSums(B), strength = rowSums(M)),
  tibble(type = "insects", species = colnames(M), degree = colSums(B), strength = colSums(M))) |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("plants", "insects")))
nodes |> group_by(type) |> slice_max(degree, n = 3)   # Apis mellifera: 46 partners

ggplot(nodes, aes(degree, fill = type)) + geom_bar() +
  facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free") + scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_plant, col_poll), guide = "none")
ggplot(nodes, aes(strength, fill = type)) + geom_histogram(bins = 25) + scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free") + scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_plant, col_poll), guide = "none")
```

```{r degree vs strength, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(nodes, aes(strength, degree, colour = type)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") + geom_count(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() + scale_colour_manual(values = c(col_plant, col_poll))
```

Specialisation index $d'$ of the plants, native vs non-native (slide *"Specialisation index
$d'$"*):

```{r dprime, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
dprime <- tibble(plant = rownames(M), dprime = dfun(M)$dprime, status = plant_status[rownames(M)]) |>
  filter(status %in% c("Native", "Non-native"))
dprime |> group_by(status) |> summarise(n = n(), median = median(dprime))
wilcox.test(dprime ~ status, data = dprime)
ggplot(dprime, aes(status, dprime)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.5, colour = col_plant) + labs(x = NULL, y = "d'")
```

## Network-level descriptors

Table of the slide *"Descriptors per city"*: connectance $C = L / (nm)$, interaction evenness
$E$, nestedness NODF.

```{r metrics}
network_metrics <- function(M) {
  B <- 1 * (M > 0); P <- M[M > 0] / sum(M)
  tibble(plants = nrow(B), insects = ncol(B), links = sum(B), visits = sum(M),
         C = round(mean(B), 3), E = round(-sum(P * log(P)) / log(sum(B)), 2),
         NODF = round(nestednodf(B)$statistic[["NODF"]], 1))
}
bind_rows(lapply(net_city, network_metrics), .id = "city") |> knitr::kable()
```

# Introduction to stochastic block models

## The simplest model: Erdős–Rényi

$Y_{ij} \sim \mathcal{B}ern(p)$, $\hat p = C$: the degrees would be Binomial.

```{r erdos renyi, fig.height = 4}
p_hat <- mean(B); p_hat
er <- bind_rows(tibble(type = "plants", degree = 0:50, expected = nrow(B) * dbinom(0:50, ncol(B), p_hat)),
                tibble(type = "insects", degree = 0:50, expected = ncol(B) * dbinom(0:50, nrow(B), p_hat))) |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("plants", "insects"))) |>
  filter(degree <= ifelse(type == "plants", max(rowSums(B)), max(colSums(B))))
ggplot(nodes, aes(degree)) + geom_bar(aes(fill = type)) +
  geom_line(data = er, aes(y = expected)) + facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_plant, col_poll), guide = "none")
```

## Bipartite SBM on simulated networks

*"One model, many structures"*: modular, core–periphery and nested structures simulated with
`sampleBipartiteSBM`, then *"What inference does"*: the groups are recovered from a matrix in
an arbitrary order.

```{r simulation, fig.height = 4}
set.seed(2)
structures <- list(
  Modular = list(alpha = matrix(c(.60, .05, .02, .03, .40, .05, .02, .04, .25), 3, byrow = TRUE),
                 pi = c(.2, .3, .5), rho = c(.25, .35, .4)),
  `Core-periphery` = list(alpha = matrix(c(.85, .45, .15, .30, .05, .01), 2, byrow = TRUE),
                          pi = c(.3, .7), rho = c(.15, .35, .5)),
  Nested = list(alpha = matrix(c(.95, .85, .70, .50, .85, .45, .15, .03, .60, .10, .02, .01), 3, byrow = TRUE),
                pi = c(.2, .3, .5), rho = c(.1, .2, .3, .4)))
sims <- lapply(structures, function(s)
  sampleBipartiteSBM(nbNodes = c(60, 90), blockProp = list(row = s$pi, col = s$rho),
                     connectParam = list(mean = s$alpha), model = "bernoulli",
                     dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "pollinators")))
wrap_plots(lapply(names(sims), function(s) plot(sims[[s]], type = "data") + ggtitle(s)))
```

```{r simulation inference, fig.height = 4}
Y <- sims$Modular$networkData
Y <- Y[sample(nrow(Y)), sample(ncol(Y))]          # arbitrary order, as observed
fit_sim <- estimateBipartiteSBM(Y, model = "bernoulli", estimOptions = list(verbosity = 0, plot = FALSE))
fit_sim$nbBlocks
plotMyMatrix(Y) + plot(fit_sim, type = "data")
```

## Application to the UK data

One bipartite SBM per city, on the counts (Poisson) and on the binary networks (Bernoulli).
`estimateBipartiteSBM` explores the numbers of groups $(K, L)$ and keeps the best ICL.

```{r sbm fits}
net_bin <- lapply(net_city, function(M) 1 * (M > 0))
sbm_opts <- list(verbosity = 0, plot = FALSE, nbCores = 4)
fit_bin <- cached_fit("results_analysis/results_city_SBM_bernoulli.rds",
  lapply(net_bin, estimateBipartiteSBM, model = "bernoulli",
         dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "insects"), estimOptions = sbm_opts))
fit_pois <- cached_fit("results_analysis/results_city_SBM_poisson.rds",
  lapply(net_city, estimateBipartiteSBM, model = "poisson",
         dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "insects"), estimOptions = sbm_opts))
```

Slide *"ICL versus BIC"*: the criteria along the explored models (Bristol, binary).

```{r icl, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
fit_bin$Bristol$storedModels |>
  mutate(K_plus_L = nbRowBlocks + nbColBlocks) |>
  pivot_longer(c(ICL, loglik), names_to = "criterion") |>
  ggplot(aes(K_plus_L, value, colour = criterion)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(ICL = col_poll, loglik = "grey55"))
```

### Bristol: SBM on the counts

```{r bristol poisson}
fp <- fit_pois$Bristol
fp$nbBlocks
# counts on a log scale, ordered by the estimated groups
plot_counts <- function(fit) plotMyMatrix(log1p(fit$networkData), dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "insects"),
  clustering = list(row = fit$memberships$plants, col = fit$memberships$insects))
plot_counts(fp)
```

The groups mostly sort species by their number of visits:

```{r poisson strength, fig.height = 4}
bind_rows(tibble(type = "plants", group = fp$memberships$plants, visits = rowSums(fp$networkData)),
          tibble(type = "insects", group = fp$memberships$insects, visits = colSums(fp$networkData))) |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("plants", "insects"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(group), visits, colour = type)) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15) +
  scale_y_log10() + facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(insects = col_poll, plants = col_plant), guide = "none") + labs(x = "group")
```

### Edinburgh: one insect drives the counts

*Reichertella geniculata*: 300 visits on *Taraxacum* at one site. The Poisson SBM with and
without this insect:

```{r edinburgh}
reich <- "Reichertella geniculata"
baldock$records |> filter(insect == reich) |> count(site, plant, sort = TRUE) |> head(3)
fit_pois_noR <- cached_fit("results_analysis/results_city_SBM_poisson_without_reichertella.rds",
  lapply(net_city, function(M) {
    M <- M[, colnames(M) != reich]
    M <- M[rowSums(M) > 0, colSums(M) > 0]          # plants visited only by this insect
    estimateBipartiteSBM(M, model = "poisson", dimLabels = c(row = "plants", col = "insects"),
                         estimOptions = sbm_opts)
  }))
c(with = fit_pois$Edinburgh$nbBlocks, without = fit_pois_noR$Edinburgh$nbBlocks)
plot_counts(fit_pois$Edinburgh) + plot_counts(fit_pois_noR$Edinburgh)
```

### Bristol: SBM on the binary network

```{r bristol bernoulli, fig.height = 4.5}
fb <- fit_bin$Bristol
fb$nbBlocks
round(fb$connectParam$mean, 2)        # alpha_kl
lapply(fb$blockProp, round, 2)         # pi_k, rho_l
plot(fb, type = "data") + plot(fb, type = "expected") + plot(fb, type = "meso")
```

Species of the core groups (*"Bristol: interpretation"*):

```{r bristol core}
core_p <- which.max(rowSums(fb$connectParam$mean)); core_i <- which.max(colSums(fb$connectParam$mean))
rownames(fb$networkData)[fb$memberships$plants == core_p]
colnames(fb$networkData)[fb$memberships$insects == core_i]
table(plants = fb$memberships$plants); table(insects = fb$memberships$insects)
```

Composition of the groups: plant status and insect group (*"Bristol: composition of the
groups"*).

```{r bristol composition, fig.height = 4}
composition <- function(group, value, cols, title) {
  tibble(group = factor(group), value = factor(value, levels = names(cols))) |>
    ggplot(aes(group, fill = value)) + geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = NULL) + labs(y = NULL, title = title)
}
composition(fb$memberships$plants, plant_status[rownames(fb$networkData)], cols_status, "plants") +
  composition(fb$memberships$insects, insect_group[colnames(fb$networkData)], cols_group, "insects")
```

### One SBM per city

```{r sbm per city}
tibble(city = names(net_city),
       Bernoulli = sapply(fit_bin, function(f) paste(f$nbBlocks, collapse = " x ")),
       Poisson = sapply(fit_pois, function(f) paste(f$nbBlocks, collapse = " x "))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r sbm per city plot, fig.height = 8}
wrap_plots(lapply(names(fit_bin), function(cc) plot(fit_bin[[cc]], type = "data") + ggtitle(cc)), nrow = 2)
```

*"Most species are seen in one city"*:

```{r n cities, fig.height = 4}
n_cities <- bind_rows(
  tibble(type = "plants", species = unlist(lapply(net_city, rownames))),
  tibble(type = "insects", species = unlist(lapply(net_city, colnames)))) |>
  count(type, species, name = "n_cities") |> mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("plants", "insects")))
table(n_cities$type, n_cities$n_cities)
ggplot(n_cities, aes(n_cities, fill = type)) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~type) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(insects = col_poll, plants = col_plant), guide = "none")
```

# Modelling collections of networks

## Application to the city networks

`estimate_colBiSBM` fits the colBiSBM on the 4 binary networks, and the separate SBMs
(`sep_BiSBM`) for comparison. Models: `iid` (same $\alpha$, same proportions), `pi` / `rho`
(free plant / insect proportions). About 30 min per model
(`scripts/fit_colSBM_cities.R`).

```{r colsbm cities}
col_fits <- lapply(c(iid = "iid", pi = "pi", rho = "rho"), function(model)
  cached_fit(paste0("results_analysis/results_city_colBiSBM_", model, ".rds"),
    estimate_colBiSBM(netlist = net_bin, colsbm_model = model, net_id = names(net_bin),
                      distribution = "bernoulli", nb_run = 3,
                      global_opts = list(nb_cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1),
                                         verbosity = 0, plot_details = 0))))
```

*"Joint or separate models?"*: the BICL of the joint models and of the separate SBMs.

```{r joint vs separate}
bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "sep-BiSBM (one per city)",
         blocks = paste(sapply(col_fits$iid$sep_BiSBM$models, function(m) paste(m$Q, collapse = "x")), collapse = ", "),
         BICL = sum(col_fits$iid$sep_BiSBM$BICL)),
  tibble(model = paste0(names(col_fits), "-colBiSBM"),
         blocks = sapply(col_fits, function(f) paste(f$best_fit$Q, collapse = " x ")),
         BICL = sapply(col_fits, function(f) f$best_fit$BICL))) |>
  mutate(BICL = round(BICL)) |> knitr::kable()
```

### The common structure

$\hat\alpha_{k\ell}$ shared by the 4 cities, with the block proportions $\hat\pi_k$, $\hat\rho_\ell$:

```{r colsbm alpha, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6}
fit <- col_fits$iid$best_fit
round(fit$alpha, 2)
lapply(fit$pi[[1]], round, 2)
plot(fit, type = "meso", values = TRUE)
```

*"The same groups in every city"*: each city reordered by the joint groups.

```{r colsbm block, fig.height = 8}
wrap_plots(lapply(seq_along(fit$net_id), function(m)
  plot(fit, type = "block", net_id = m) + ggtitle(fit$net_id[m])), nrow = 2)
```

The joint groups of each species in each city:

```{r memberships}
groups <- extract_nodes_groups(fit) |>
  mutate(type = ifelse(node_type == "row", "plant", "insect"),
         value = ifelse(type == "plant", plant_status[node_name], insect_group[node_name])) |>
  rename(city = network, species = node_name, block = cluster)
head(groups)
```

*"Joint modelling: more statistical power"*: number of species of each plant group per city
(P1: 1 to 3 species per city).

```{r group sizes}
groups |> filter(type == "plant") |> count(city, block = paste0("P", block)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = block, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

*"The 4 cities: composition of the groups"* (a species seen in 2 cities counts twice):

```{r colsbm composition, fig.height = 4.5}
with(filter(groups, type == "plant"), composition(paste0("P", block), value, cols_status, "plants: status")) +
  with(filter(groups, type == "insect", !is.na(value)),
       composition(paste0("I", block), value, cols_group, "insects: group"))
```

*"The same composition as in Bristol?"*: the Bristol groups (separate SBM) vs the joint groups.

```{r bristol vs joint}
g_bristol <- filter(groups, city == "Bristol")
table(separate = fb$memberships$plants[match(g_bristol$species[g_bristol$type == "plant"], rownames(fb$networkData))],
      joint = g_bristol$block[g_bristol$type == "plant"])
table(separate = fb$memberships$insects[match(g_bristol$species[g_bristol$type == "insect"], colnames(fb$networkData))],
      joint = g_bristol$block[g_bristol$type == "insect"])
```

### Does a species keep its group across cities?

For each species seen in 2 cities and each pair of cities: its group in the two cities.

```{r moves}
pairs_cities <- inner_join(groups, groups, by = c("type", "species"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(city.x < city.y)
pairs_cities |> group_by(type) |> summarise(same_group = mean(block.x == block.y))
with(filter(pairs_cities, type == "plant"), table(pmin(block.x, block.y), pmax(block.x, block.y)))
with(filter(pairs_cities, type == "insect"), table(pmin(block.x, block.y), pmax(block.x, block.y)))
```

*"The insects that change group"*:

```{r insects changing, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 7}
changing <- groups |> filter(type == "insect") |> group_by(species) |>
  filter(n() > 1, n_distinct(block) > 1) |> mutate(mean_block = mean(block)) |> ungroup()
c(changing = n_distinct(changing$species),
  seen_in_several_cities = sum(table(groups$species[groups$type == "insect"]) > 1))
ggplot(changing, aes(city, reorder(species, -mean_block), fill = paste0("I", block))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = paste0("I", block)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(I1 = "#D45E00", I2 = "#F5A26B", I3 = "#FBE3D0"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))
```

*"Ecological messages"* and *"A nested backbone"*: the core groups hold species seen in
many cities, the peripheral groups species seen in 1 or 2 cities.

```{r ecological messages}
groups |> left_join(n_cities |> mutate(type = sub("s$", "", type)), by = c("type", "species")) |>
  group_by(type, block) |>
  summarise(n = n(), seen_in_4_cities = round(mean(n_cities == 4), 2), .groups = "drop")
groups |> filter(type == "plant", block <= 2) |> count(block, species, sort = TRUE) |> head(10)
```

## Application to the land uses

One network per land use, pooled over the 4 cities (*"The 9 land-use networks"*):

```{r landuses}
net_lu <- lapply(baldock$net_landuse, function(M) 1 * (M > 0))
tibble(land_use = names(net_lu), visits = sapply(baldock$net_landuse, sum),
       plants = sapply(net_lu, nrow), insects = sapply(net_lu, ncol),
       connectance = round(sapply(net_lu, mean), 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(visits)) |> knitr::kable()
```

`clusterize_bipartite_networks` looks for a partition of the networks into groups, each
modelled by its own colBiSBM (divisive algorithm, score = sum of the BICL of the groups).
The scores of all the steps (the trees of the slides) are printed during the fit with
`verbosity = 1`; the result keeps the final partition.

```{r clustering function}
partition_table <- function(clu) {
  bind_rows(lapply(clu$partition, function(p) tibble(
    group = paste(p$best_fit$net_id, collapse = ", "),
    blocks = paste(p$best_fit$Q, collapse = " x "), BICL = round(p$best_fit$BICL, 1)))) |>
    mutate(score = sum(BICL))
}
opts_clu <- list(nb_cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), verbosity = 1, plot_details = 0)
```

### The 9 land uses ($\pi\rho$-colBiSBM)

About 1.5 h (`scripts/fit_colSBM_landuse.R`).

```{r clustering 9}
clu9 <- cached_fit("results_analysis/results_landuse_colBiSBM_clustering_pirho.rds",
  clusterize_bipartite_networks(netlist = net_lu, colsbm_model = "pirho", net_id = names(net_lu),
                                nb_run = 3, global_opts = opts_clu))
clu9$clustering_history
partition_table(clu9) |> knitr::kable()
```

### Without the 3 small land uses (iid-colBiSBM)

Other greenspace, Pavement and Man-made surface removed. About 10 min
(`scripts/fit_colSBM_landuse6_clustering.R`).

```{r clustering 6}
landuses6 <- c("Allotment", "Cemetery", "Garden", "Nature reserve", "Park", "Verge")
clu6 <- cached_fit("results_analysis/results_landuse6_colBiSBM_clustering_iid.rds",
  clusterize_bipartite_networks(netlist = net_lu[landuses6], colsbm_model = "iid", net_id = landuses6,
                                nb_run = 3, global_opts = opts_clu))
clu6$clustering_history
partition_table(clu6) |> knitr::kable()
fits6 <- lapply(clu6$partition, function(p) p$best_fit)
names(fits6) <- ifelse(sapply(fits6, function(f) "Cemetery" %in% f$net_id), "greenspaces", "gardened")
```

### Two different structures

Graphon view (*"Two different structures: graphon view"*) and $\hat\alpha$ of each group:

```{r landuse graphon, fig.height = 4.5}
plot(fits6$greenspaces, type = "graphon") + ggtitle("Cemetery, Nature reserve, Park, Verge") +
  plot(fits6$gardened, type = "graphon") + ggtitle("Allotment, Garden")
```

```{r landuse alpha, fig.height = 5}
lapply(fits6, function(f) round(f$alpha, 2))
plot(fits6$greenspaces, type = "meso", values = TRUE) | plot(fits6$gardened, type = "meso", values = TRUE)
```

### Greenspaces: a core–periphery

```{r greenspaces}
g_green <- extract_nodes_groups(fits6$greenspaces) |>
  mutate(type = ifelse(node_type == "row", "plant", "insect"),
         value = ifelse(type == "plant", plant_status[node_name], insect_group[node_name]))
# plants of the two core groups (all land uses pooled), with their status
g_green |> filter(type == "plant", cluster <= 2) |> distinct(cluster, node_name, value) |> arrange(cluster)
# insect groups: composition
g_green |> filter(type == "insect") |> count(cluster, value) |> group_by(cluster) |>
  mutate(p = round(n / sum(n), 2)) |> select(-n) |> pivot_wider(names_from = value, values_from = p, values_fill = 0)
```

### Gardens: bee flowers vs fly flowers

```{r gardens}
g_gard <- extract_nodes_groups(fits6$gardened) |>
  mutate(type = ifelse(node_type == "row", "plant", "insect"),
         value = ifelse(type == "plant", plant_status[node_name], insect_group[node_name]))
g_gard |> filter(type == "plant") |> count(cluster, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = value, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
# insects in I2 in one land use and in I3 in the other
g_gard |> filter(type == "insect") |> group_by(node_name) |>
  filter(n() == 2, n_distinct(cluster) == 2) |> ungroup() |> count(network, cluster)
```
